transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2028-02-14 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Recording ID: ff-20280214-4829

AUTO SUMMARY: quick check-in about annual renewal and adding eu edge + dedicated pool, some action items on pricing + benchmarks

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, is this still a good 48 minutes?
[00:07] Aaron Vega: Yeah sounds good. we've got Chris from procurement and Sofia from ML ops on the line.
[00:12] Maya Chen: perfect. quick round — i'll kick off with what we'll cover: renewal terms, capacity uplift, adding an EU edge region, and then technical next steps for the pilot benchmarks. Luis will run through the benchmark plan. Priya will cover onboarding and procurement asks.
[00:28] Luis Ortega: hi all, hey — quick note i put together a short test plan, it's in the deck link i just posted — (link: drive.redwood.io/galactic/bench-2028). good to run some smoke now and a 24h hammer test once you give the prod prompt set.
[00:42] Sofia Petrov: cool — we can provide the prompt set, it's about 120k tokens daily on peak. latency target is p95 <= 180ms for single-turn gen on 2k token contexts, that is our SLA hope.
[00:55] Aaron Vega: right and also we need EU residency for the user data; we can't have any unencrypted logs leave EU.
[01:02] Maya Chen: understood. so two things: we can deploy an EU edge region on Redwood Private or in Dedicated in EU tenancy depending on your preference. for hosted we do have options but residency controls are limited.
[01:17] Chris Nolan: procurement question — if we extend 12 months and commit to 20% uplift now, what does the pricing look like — can you give a quick delta?
[01:28] Maya Chen: short answer: committed reserved capacity reduces unit price by about 18-22% vs on-demand hosted. if you add an EU edge and dedicated pool there's a baseline infra premium — roughly 8-12% depending on GPU class and quantization profile. i'll send a spreadsheet with tiered options.
[01:46] Aaron Vega: Sofia, do you prefer dedicated all in EU or split us + eu?
[01:52] Sofia Petrov: For latency and failover, we prefer a split — primary EU for EU traffic, US primary for Americas. but the KV cache behavior is a concern — warm cache vs cold when failing over between regions, anything to call out?
[02:08] Luis Ortega: yeah good call, cache is per-runtime so cold-starts can add a few hundred ms, we typically recommend prefix caching and sticky routing for sessions to keep cache warm. for cross-region failover we support automated fallback but you'll see a small latency blip while KV warms. we can simulate this in the 24h test.
[02:31] Maya Chen: on security, do you require a private control plane? i.e., Redwood Private with customer VPC?
[02:39] Aaron Vega: for EU they want customer-managed networking and their own KMS. SOC2 is also table stakes.
[02:44] Priya Raman: note — we have an enterprise package that includes Private deployment, KMS integration, and audit log retention. i can share the SOC2 artifact and the KMS integration guide.
[02:55] Chris Nolan: how long does Private onboarding typically take? our legal team wants to know the ramp window.
[03:00] Priya Raman: typical is 6-10 weeks from signed SOW for EU on-premish private with our template, might be shorter if you already have network peering in place — less than 8 usually for standard patterns.
[03:14] Aaron Vega: ok procurement timeline is end of feb for PO if possible.
[03:18] Maya Chen: that syncs well with a 12-month extension start date of 2028-03-01. if procurement can issue PO by 2028-02-28 we can schedule capacity and order GPUs.
[03:30] Sofia Petrov: question about SLA — if we choose dedicated, do you guarantee latency SLO or just throughput?
[03:37] Luis Ortega: with dedicated we can offer latency SLOs at the cluster level tuned for your model and seq-length profile. we instrument token-level metrics and can set alerting for regressions. important to note the SLO assumes certain batch sizes and KV hit rates — dev workload pattern affects realized latency.
[03:58] Aaron Vega: are there any caveats on model variant compatibility? we use an LLaMA-derived open model with custom fine-tunes.
[04:05] Luis Ortega: that's fine — we support custom weights and fine-tuned checkpoints. for dedicated you'd bring the model to our serving runtime; we may recommend a quantized variant for cost savings, but we'll run side-by-side qual checks. there might be performance differences to evaluate.
[04:27] Maya Chen: okay let's talk pricing tiers — i'll be high level now: option A: 12-month extension, 20% capacity uplift, Hosted with reserved nodes, B: 12-month + Dedicated EU pool (baseline premium), C: 24-month enterprise extension with Private deployment (lowest unit price but higher upfront).
[04:49] Chris Nolan: procurement likes predictable monthly charges — option C sounds good but need capex signoff.
[04:56] Aaron Vega: if option B reduces tail latency and we get EU residency, i'm leaning there.
[05:02] Sofia Petrov: also we need tracing hooks and per-request user id in audit logs — to debug chain-of-thought outputs. is that supported?
[05:11] Luis Ortega: yes we can surface per-request metadata, token-level cost breakdown, and request/response traces (redacted if you want). audit logs integrate with your SIEM via S3 or streaming; we can show the schema.
[05:26] Maya Chen: i'm going to hand it to Luis to walk through the benchmark plan and the data we need from you.
[05:31] Luis Ortega: right. plan: 1) smoke test with your 1k prompt sample, 2) 8-hour warm run with realistic traffic to validate p95/p99, 3) 24h hammer test to validate autoscaling/burst and KV behavior, 4) failover simulation EU->US and measure cold-cache penalty. want to capture token counts, latencies, kv hit rates, and GPU util traces. send us the prompt set and a redacted traffic profile.
[06:00] Sofia Petrov: can we anonymize logs? we can't send PII.
[06:04] Luis Ortega: yes — we only need inputs hashed or redacted, and we can sign an NDA addendum if necessary.
[06:10] Chris Nolan: on the PO side, what payment terms do you offer? net30? net45?
[06:15] Maya Chen: standard is net30 for new enterprise, but we can negotiate net45 for longer commitments. procurement note logged.
[06:23] Aaron Vega: what about failover cost — if we have traffic routed to a different region during outage, is there a cross-region billing surcharge?
[06:31] Maya Chen: cross-region traffic can incur egress and also potential compute, if you need standby capacity reserved in both regions that costs more. we can design a fallback that uses smaller standby pool to reduce cost — Luis will propose a policy.
[06:46] Luis Ortega: yes we can use tiered burst: primary pool handles steady-state, burst pool activates on spikes; cold-warmed cache approach for standby. we'll include cost simulation in the benchmark readout.
[07:00] (pause, typing sounds)
[07:10] Sofia Petrov: quick technical: our fine-tune is 7B parameters but uses long context up to 4k tokens — any limitations?
[07:18] Luis Ortega: 4k is supported by our runtime. for 7B seq-length throughput is good; the tradeoff is memory usage for KV and batch size. for your 120k tokens/day peak we should be fine in the suggested pool.
[07:33] Aaron Vega: are there any potential feature gaps like function calling or structured outputs we depend on?
[07:40] Maya Chen: we support function/tool calling patterns and structured JSON outputs; sometimes NLU wrappers or prompt engineering is needed for deterministic formats. we can run eval prompts as part of the pilot.
[07:55] Chris Nolan: legal wanted to confirm we get audit logs for model version changes and who called what.
[08:01] Priya Raman: yes audit trails include model deployments, rollouts, and user-level access logs. with KMS we can also provide key rotation records.
[08:12] Aaron Vega: ok good. question: timeline for adding EU edge region if we sign by the end of feb?
[08:20] Priya Raman: if PO by 2028-02-28 we can provision a staging geocluster in EU by mid-March and do validation tests, production go-live late March/early April. Private onboarding might push that a few weeks.
[08:37] Luis Ortega: note re: benchmarking environment — we'll provision equivalent GPU class (A100-ish) but final hardware depends on capacity available at provisioning time.
[08:49] Maya Chen: any blockers on your side for going ahead with the 12-month + 20% uplift proposal?
[08:55] Aaron Vega: procurement needs finalized numbers to sign but engineering wants to see bench results first.
[09:00] Chris Nolan: yes procurement will need the revised MSA and pricing.
[09:05] Maya Chen: fair — i'll push pricing and a draft contract by Friday. that will include an option to upgrade to Private within 90 days if needed.
[09:15] Sofia Petrov: can you also include a clause for a canary rollout and fallback policy? we want a clear rollback path.
[09:21] Maya Chen: absolutely. our rollouts support canary by traffic percentage and automatic fallback if error rates exceed thresholds. we'll include the policy in SOW.
[09:33] Luis Ortega: one more technical note — quantization: if we quantize to int8 we get about 35-45% cost reduction typically, but it's model-dependent; we'll run quantized vs fp16 runs in the pilot. expect slight quality deltas.
[09:50] Aaron Vega: quality vs cost — we need a threshold where quality regression triggers rollback.
[09:55] Maya Chen: we'll capture evaluation metrics on the prompt set and create a quality gate; if metric drops exceed agreed delta we'll fall back to prior variant.
[10:06] (short cross-talk)
[10:12] Chris Nolan: procurement timeline again — i'll try to expedite PO by 2/28 if we get the numbers and draft.
[10:18] Maya Chen: excellent. so recap of next steps: Maya send pricing & draft SOW; Luis run bench with prompt set to validate latency/cost; Priya schedule onboarding deep-dive; customer confirm KMS vendor and procurement timeline.
[10:34] Aaron Vega: sounds good. thanks all.
[10:37] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and scheduling invites.
[10:42] (meeting ends)

NOTES: transcript contains some mis-heard words and auto-attribution errors; customers asked for 24h hammer test, quantization comparison, and explicit canary/rollback policy.
